transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-26
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Stone (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Leah Ortega (CTO, Hearthbridge), Samir Patel (Lead ML Engineer), Jordan Kim (Platform)
Shared links: redwood-hosting-options.pdf, hearthbridge-benchmark-inputs.csv, redwood-soc2-pack.zip, quickstart-first-token.md

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Hearthbridge is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: PLG/self-serve for early product experimentation (time-to-first-token important) with the option to move some workloads to Dedicated or Private (VPC) for PII-sensitive flows. Primary concerns: latency targets for chat (sub-200ms tail), cost per 1k tokens for high-throughput inference, auditability (audit logs/SSO), KMS integration, and rollout strategy. Next steps include micro-benchmarks, sharing security artifacts, and activating free credits for a pilot.

Topics: hosting modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), free credits & quickstart flow, time-to-first-token, routing policies (latency vs cost), KV/prefix caching, KMS + audit logs, pilot scope and success metrics.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I am Maya from Redwood, Derek and Priya are on from SE.
[00:10] Leah Ortega: Leah here, hi. Samir and Jordan also on.
[00:15] Derek Stone: Hey, great to meet you all. Real quick agenda — understand Hearthbridge constraints, run through hosting options, and discuss a short pilot and TTFT (time-to-first-token) expectations.
[00:30] Jordan Kim: Sounds good. We mainly want to understand: can we start self-serve with credits and fast proof-of-concept and then, depending on data sensitivity, route specific requests to a Private VPC?
[00:42] Priya Anand: Yep that's a common pattern. Redwood supports same API across Hosted, Dedicated and Private, so code-level changes are minimal. For routing you can set policy rules — latency-first for chat, cost-first for background embeddings — and automatic fallbacks.
[01:05] Samir Patel: When you say "automatic fallback" do you mean you can downgrade model variant automatically if capacity is constrained?
[01:12] Derek Stone: Exactly, we can route to a quantized variant or a cheaper instance group. There's also per-route model pinning. Important to note though, output QoL might shift slightly with quantization — we'll show you the evals.
[01:30] Leah Ortega: Our immediate KPI is response time for customer-facing chat — targeting ~150ms median and keeping 99th under 250ms if possible. How feasible on Hosted?
[01:42] Derek Stone: For short contexts and a production-optimized model, hosted can hit those medians in most regions. Tail depends on your RPS distribution and sequence lengths. We often recommend prefix/KV caching for common prompts to knock down token generation time on the critical path.
[02:05] Jordan Kim: KV cache sounds good; is that supported for private deployments as well?
[02:10] Priya Anand: Yes, cache is an execution feature in the runtime — included across modes. For Private, cache can be colocated in your VPC; for Hosted it's managed but configurable TTLs.
[02:26] Samir Patel: Talking about data, we have traces that include PII in some messages. We need KMS, audit logs, and SSO. Also retention policies. SOC 2 is a must.
[02:40] Maya Chen: Understood — we have SOC 2 artifacts and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and network controls. We'll share the SOC2 pack and KMS docs after this call.
[03:00] Leah Ortega: Great. From a procurement perspective, what's the path to a pilot? Free credits, then Dedicated reserve or private contract?
[03:10] Maya Chen: Typical flow: we activate credits for a self-serve account (PLG) so your engineers can get TTFT, run a quick experiment. Parallelly SEs can run a micro-benchmark with your prompts to estimate cost & latency. If you need commit-backed performance we move to Dedicated; Private is a separate contract for data isolation.
[03:30] Derek Stone: For the micro-benchmark we'll need a sample prompt set and target RPS profile — ideally the 95th percentile of your expected load. Samir, could you share a ~300-line sample CSV?
[03:40] Samir Patel: Yeah I can do that. I'll sanitize PII first.
[03:44] Jordan Kim: How long does it take to get initial tokens flowing in self-serve? Our devs hate long onboarding.
[03:50] Maya Chen: Typical TTFT is minutes to an hour: sign up, API key creation, run the quickstart script. We'll send a step-by-step 'first-token' guide. Also we can pre-provision credits so your team can jump straight into testing.
[04:07] Leah Ortega: Are there rate limits on the trial credits? We want fair testing without getting throttled too early.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We'll set reasonable quotas; for the micro-benchmark we can temporarily increase them. If you choose Dedicated that's predictable throughput with committed capacity.
[04:23] Samir Patel: Quick question on observability: do you expose per-token breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and tracing? We need integration with our internal monitoring.
[04:33] Priya Anand: Redwood Console has per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks you can forward to your Sentry/NewRelic. You can also pull logs via the API and ship to your logging destination.
[04:50] Jordan Kim: About data residency: some EU customers require data to never leave region. Does Hosted provide region selection?
[04:58] Derek Stone: Yes, we have region selection in hosted; plus Private deployments can be entirely in your VPC or on-prem so resident constraints are satisfied.
[05:10] Leah Ortega: And compliance — retention windows, ability to delete customer transcripts?
[05:16] Maya Chen: You can configure retention and we support delete-on-demand. In Private, all logs live in your network. We'll include retention feature notes in the SOC2 packet.
[05:30] Samir Patel: On the model side — will Redwood manage model updates or do we pin to a version? We need reproducible outputs for some batch jobs.
[05:39] Priya Anand: You can pin model versions per-route to ensure reproducibility, and we support rollouts/canaries for safe upgrades. We'll document the versioning scheme in the model catalog.
[05:55] Leah Ortega: Cost question — for embedding-heavy workloads, we have high throughput but don't need sub-200ms latency. Can we route embeddings to lower-cost variants?
[06:04] Derek Stone: Absolutely. Policy-based routing lets you send embeddings to cheaper instance pools or quantized models, letting chat go to the low-latency pool.
[06:15] Samir Patel: Do you provide guidance on quantization choices for accuracy tradeoffs? We care about retrieval quality.
[06:20] Priya Anand: Redwood Optimize gives quantization recommendations by workload and returns expected QoL impact. Plus our evals show embedding drift metrics. We'll share a short note and examples.
[06:35] Jordan Kim: Sounds good. I want to talk briefly about networking and ingress. For Private, do you host the control plane or is that customer-managed?
[06:44] Maya Chen: Control plane remains hosted for managed Private deployments but the data plane can be customer-managed in your VPC or on-prem. For air-gapped setups we have an on-prem package.
[06:56] Leah Ortega: What's the path for an enterprise SSO integration for our org?
[07:01] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC controls. We'll share our SSO integration guide.
[07:12] Samir Patel: For benchmarking — what metrics do you collect server-side we can reference? Token latency, decode time, GPU utilization?
[07:21] Derek Stone: We can capture per-token generation time, queue latency, instance-level GPU metrics and export them. For your micro-benchmark we'll produce a short report with median/99th latency and cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[07:40] Leah Ortega: Ok, pilot success criteria I'd propose: 1) get devs to first token within 1 hour, 2) achieve median chat latency <180ms for the sample workload, 3) cost estimate within 20% of SE projection.
[07:55] Maya Chen: That's useful — we'll align the pilot to those metrics.
[08:05] Jordan Kim: Anything special around security scanning or pen tests? Our security team will want to run a questionnaire.
[08:12] Priya Anand: We regularly provide security questionnaires and can aggregate answers in a single package. For deeper security reviews we engage Solutions Engineering.
[08:25] Samir Patel: One other question — do you have a hosted model catalog, or do we bring our own models if we run private?
[08:33] Derek Stone: Both. Hosted includes a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified profiles. In Private, you can host your model artifacts (we support common formats) and the runtime supports them. If you want we can evaluate your model for performance.
[08:50] Leah Ortega: Okay, switching to timeline: we'd like to have a pilot in February and then decide Q2 for Dedicated or Private. Any blockers?
[08:58] Maya Chen: No blockers on our side. We'll prepare credits and an SE-led benchmark.
[09:06] Samir Patel: For the micro-benchmark, do you emulate KV/prefix caching or do we need to mock it?
[09:12] Derek Stone: We can run two passes: cold start (no cache) and warm (with prefix cache applied) so you see the real end-to-end numbers.
[09:25] Jordan Kim: Will we be billed for the benchmark?
[09:28] Maya Chen: No, we'll use the pilot credits for the benchmark.
[09:33] Leah Ortega: Could you clarify retention & logs for Hosted during pilot? We prefer minimal retention of any PII.
[09:40] Priya Anand: We'll set retention policy to minimum and redact or exclude transcripts as needed. We'll include the config steps in the shared docs.
[09:50] Samir Patel: On the SDKs: we have a Node.js backend. Is the quickstart SDK first-class for that stack?
[09:57] Derek Stone: Yes, we have official Node and Python SDKs and example repos. Quickstart script creates a small express app that calls the Redwood API. We'll send the repo link.
[10:08] Maya Chen: I'll enumerate next steps in email: share SOC2 pack and KMS docs, activate credits, run a benchmark (SE), and schedule pilot kickoff.
[10:18] Leah Ortega: Perfect. Any commercial questions right now?
[10:21] Maya Chen: Not yet — pilots are typically covered by credits and then we can discuss Dedicated pricing if you move to reserve capacity.
[10:26] (discussion continues — skipping a chunk to capture middle-to-end timing)

[22:30] Derek Stone: Jumping back — one technical note: if your generation lengths average 40 tokens, throughput and batching behave differently than 200 token use cases. Please include sequence length histograms in the sample CSV.
[22:45] Samir Patel: Will do.
[23:05] Jordan Kim: Any recommended quantization profile for our retrieval-augmented generation flows? We want minimal semantic drift.
[23:12] Priya Anand: For RAG we usually suggest int8 with per-channel calibration for embeddings, and a slightly higher-bit profile for the decoder part — but we'll provide the exact guidance after seeing the evals.
[24:00] Leah Ortega: On billing — will the early pilot be simple prepaid credits? We need a PO sometimes for procurement.
[24:08] Maya Chen: We can invoice for credits if needed. We'll coordinate with finance.
[24:20] Samir Patel: About fallbacks — if the model variant changes, how are clients informed? Do you surface headers or an event?
[24:27] Derek Stone: Fallbacks are transparent at the routing layer but we can emit a trace event to the request logs and post a webhook to your monitoring if you want explicit signals.
[24:42] Jordan Kim: Nice. For Private deployments, how long does provisioning take?
[24:48] Priya Anand: Small Private deployments can be scheduled in a few weeks depending on networking approvals. On-prem air-gapped can be longer.
[24:58] Leah Ortega: Ok, I think we have enough. Can we recap the explicit next steps?
[25:05] Maya Chen: Sure. 1) Maya to send SOC2/KMS/docs and quickstart guide and pre-activate credits. 2) Samir to send sanitized sample prompts and RPS/seq-length histogram. 3) Derek to run micro-benchmark and return latency/cost report. 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for week of Feb 8.
[25:25] Samir Patel: I'll get the CSV by Friday.
[25:28] Leah Ortega: I'll loop in procurement about PO options.
[25:31] Jordan Kim: And I'll review network requirements for VPC private path.
[25:35] Priya Anand: We'll also attach a short note on model pinning and rollback policies.
[25:40] Maya Chen: Great. Any final questions?
[25:45] Leah Ortega: Not for me. Thanks all.
[25:49] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and credits today.

(brief wrap, call ends)
